contentText:
Take a look back at our main image again; see that in the background? That's the North America Nebula that I photographed with the Vaonis Vespera Pro 2 as part of my recent testing. I was massively impressed, both by its performance and the fact that this new smart telescope is currently on sale at its lowest-ever price for Black Friday 2026.

I would expect this level of astrophotography from huge observatories and space telescopes, not from a consumer smart telescope. After setting up the Vespera Pro 2 for just an hour in my backyard, I was blown away by the resulting image.

Vespera Pro 2: was $2990 now $2490
This is the second release of the Vaonis Vespera Pro. Just like the original, it has a 12.5MP sensor, 225GB internal storage, a built-in hygrometer and 11-hour battery life, but with some changes. The optical design has been upgraded to increase sharpness, direct USB-C file transfer and ships with an adjustable carbon fiber tripod.

We gave the original 4.5/5 stars in our Vaonis Vespera Pro review.

The Vespera Pro 2 is virtually identical to the first model apart from an upgraded interior. Harry Bennett / Future The touch power button glows red when turned on. Harry Bennett / Future The 50mm aperture remains the same but adds an upgraded optical design and internal light baffling. Harry Bennett / Future Separate filters are available for the Vespera Pro 2 and I would highly recommend the dual-band filter for nebula imaging. Harry Bennett / Future It's an impressive balance Vaonis have struck here between usability and premium astrophotography output. Prior to the pro-line of Vespera smart telescopes, I would have thought that this quality of astrophotography would require the highest levels of astronomy knowledge, alongside a pricey lineup of separate instruments. Don't get me wrong, the Vespera Pro 2 is not cheap but it really does have everything you need for capturing the wonders of the night sky with ease.

Operation is controlled from the Singularity app on a smart device and setup takes minutes. After connecting the telescope, simply click on your chosen target to start automatic location and imaging. The app is intuitive and helpful for beginners, suggesting a range of night sky targets that are observable from your location and customisable plans that allow you to set a range of targets for automatic imaging throughout the night, so you can get some rest.

We wrote about an early Black Friday deal on the the Vaonis Vespera Pro last week when it dropped in price, but Vaonis has now made both models of their Vespera Pro the same price. If you were thinking of getting a pro smart telescope for highly detailed nebula photography, you may as well get the better version. It comes with a fully adjustable tripod, enhanced data transfer and an overhauled optical design for maximum performance.

The Dark Shark nebula, as imaged by the Vaonis Vespera Pro 2. Harry Bennett / Future The Seahorse Nebula, as imaged by the Vaonis Vespera Pro 2. Harry Bennett / Future This is a great model for expanding your knowledge of different types of objects in the universe. Do you know what a dark nebula is? I didn't until I decided to try and image one with the Vespera Pro 2. My attempts are not the best, but you can make out the clouds of dark dust that block out starlight behind them in the Dark Shark Nebula and the Seahorse Nebula. I'm sure that if I set these targets for "multi-night observation" in the app, those images would keep getting stronger and more detailed.

The Cygnus Loop, as imaged by the Vaonis Vespera Pro 2. (Image credit: Harry Bennett / Future) On top of continuing observations from past sessions, the Vespera Pro 2 also offers mosaic mode for expanding your field of view on a certain target. This means that you can image vast expanses of the night sky without having to manually stitch together all the frames yourself. The Vespera Pro 2 does it for you. Here is my attempt at capturing the monumental supernova remnant, The Cygnus Loop. Again, it is fairly faint apart from the Eastern and Western Veil nebulas, but enabling multi-night observation will keep adding to this image whenever you get the chance to pick up where you left off.

Key features: 50mm aperture, quadruplet apochromatic optics, hard case, adjustable tripod, 12.5 MP Sony IMX676 sensor (up to 50 MP via CovalENS live mosaic), built-in hygrometer dew-control sensor, lens cap, anti-theft system, 225GB internal storage, 4000+ object database in Singularity app.
